title: Honest Minimax Regret for Positivity-Free Odds Policies near the One-Half Cap
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field).
gap_reasons: The result is confined to the highly structured class with known balanced scalar design, one-sided propensity range, Lipschitz observed moments, and a one-dimensional odds-multiplier action set; it does not establish the frontier on Zhao et al.'s broader policy model.
The diabetic-medication discussion remains only a policy-question analogy, with no data analysis or verification that the benchmark design, smoothness, or binding-boundary geometry applies there.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 produced a closed informal proof graph for finite-sample honest odds-policy selection, the exact cap-one-half elbow, and a moving-cap minimax interpolation, with a resolved fixed-cap boundary law. The final D0.5 math and rubric panels passed with no findings, but the novelty score ceiling of 7.1 placed the result at subfield below the field floor. Formalization was not started; extending the upper frontier beyond the benchmark class or validating the medical application remains future work.
tldr: The uniformly honest minimax frontier now interpolates sharply across caps approaching one half.  Writing \(u_n=1/2+a_n\), uniformly for \(0\leq a_n\leq1/32\) the explicit buffered cross-fitted observed-moment selector and an all-randomized-selector converse give the matched rate \(\sqrt{a_n^2+n^{-1/2}}-a_n\).  Thus \(a_n=o(n^{-1/4})\) retains the endpoint \(n^{-1/4}\) rate, \(a_n\asymp n^{-1/4}\) is the crossover, and \(a_n\gg n^{-1/4}\) gives \(n^{-1/2}/a_n\) up to constants; every fixed cap in \((1/2,3/4)\) remains root-sample.  Caps below one half are infeasible and caps at least three quarters are fairness-vacuous.  These finite-sample \(0.95\)-honest upper bounds hold on the strict benchmark subclass \(\mathcal P_L\); the retained cap \(2/3\) theorem still supplies the joint selected-root law and limiting one-half unbuffered violation probability.
gap: ZhaoChambazJosseYang2024 supplies the incremental odds policy, its positivity-free causal-value identification from the observed marginal, and a high-level asymptotic regret result for a generic estimated constraint, but not a finite-sample law-uniform guarantee for \(|D_P(\widehat\delta)|\le b\), unconditional expected regret, an explicit histogram construction, or a minimax converse over randomized honest selectors. Other constrained-policy work imposes overlap, regularizes fairness, or uses asymptotic candidate-wise bounds.
fill: The project isolates the full-data law to the identification step, formulates the statistical class as compatible observed marginals, derives the signed and absolute parity identities from the observed-law definitions, builds a cross-fitted histogram estimator on an explicit positive-fold split with a deterministic two-sided buffer, proves samplewise regret transfer off the confidence event, and uses two nearby observed laws with one common independent auxiliary law to lower-bound every randomized selector honest for the absolute constraint.
